newsitem.title: ROMANIA: ROMANIAN OTC MARKET GETS MORE STOCKS.
newsitem.headline: ROMANIAN OTC MARKET GETS MORE STOCKS.

text.p: Romania's over-the-counter (OTC) trading system RASDAQ said on Friday another 267 companies were expected to join in trading next week, putting the total number of traded stocks to 387.

The newcomers, including companies from all of Romania's 41 counties and covering almost all industrial sectors, were privatised under a mass selloff, which offered Romanians stakes of up to 60 percent in 4,000 state companies against privatisation paper.
The RASDAQ, which this week celebrated one month of operation, was created under a U.S. Agency for Internatiopnal Development capital market project to trade around 5,000 stocks in the long term.

Brokers said the OTC market had gained ground rapidly, with the number of stocks rising to 120 from six in the first week and turnover going up to 376 million lei this week from a modest 8.9 million when it started in October.
"Daily turnover on the OTC market is often higher than what the stock exchange makes in a week," one broker said.
Bursa de Valori Bucuresti, Romania's first bourse in 50 years, opened last November and has been hit by sluggish trading of late. It trades 15 stocks in two weekly sessions.

Officials say there is no competition between the two arms of the capital market. "The bourse is a market for higher capitalisation stocks. It is for the elite," an official said. ($=3,509 lei) -- Luli Popescu, Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
